newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water aims for real dividend growth.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water aims for real dividend growth.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Thames Water Plc said on Tuesday that its new businesses should produce a strong earnings stream and it should maintain real dividend growth.
Annual pretax profits before exceptional items were up 19 percent to 384 million pounds ($628.3 million) and paid out a total dividend of 34.4 pence per share, up 22 percent.
The company, which has one of the highest leakage levels in the country, said it had cut the amount of water seeping out of pipes by a quarter since a peak in 1995 and aimed to halve leakage by 2000.
But it warned that rainfall in the area had been low in the last year and "without significant amounts of rain in the next few weeks, it will become more difficult to avoid restrictions."

Britain is suffering its worst drought for 200 years and the new Labour government has set out a 10-point plan, including mandatory leakage targets, for companies as well as putting them in its sights for a planned tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities.

Thames said it had "responded positively" to the government's drought plans and said it hoped to establish "a constructive relationship" with government, but added that it hoped future investment levels were not "put at risk by an excessive windfall tax levy."
